script: Spread and total were not saved for Ravens-Falcons, so this Week 5 BAL@ATL script is form-only. Atlanta's last three are a Bijan Robinson ground game (64 carries, 411 yards) with Brian Robinson Jr. on 35/163, because Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. is -0.41 EPA/dropback unblitzed and the Ravens blitz only 31%. Baltimore's shape is Derrick Henry volume (65 carries, 230 yards) plus Lamar Jackson, who is fine without a blitz (0.33 EPA) against a Falcons blitz rate of just 23%. Atlanta should keep handing it off; Henry's explosives should die against Atlanta's 2.99 YPC run defense.
who_goes_off: Against the Ravens, Bijan Robinson should go off on the ground: 411 Falcons rush yards and 6.42 YPC over three games into a Baltimore defense allowing 3.91 YPC and 11 runs of 10-plus. If Baltimore's 31% blitz rate is the only way Penix functions (0.12 EPA vs blitz), Falcons WR Drake London (341 yards on 21 targets) is the pass spillover. For Baltimore, Mark Andrews (18 targets, 100 yards) fits the Falcons' middle (8.86 YPA), not an outside wideout into Atlanta's 5.23 YPA right side.
weak_spot: The Falcons' hole is the middle, not outside corners: Atlanta allows 8.86 YPA on 22 middle attempts versus 5.23 YPA on 78 right and 6.45 on 78 left, while the Falcons run defense is a wall (2.99 YPC, 2 runs of 10-plus in four games). The Ravens' hole for this Atlanta offense is the run and the chunk run, Baltimore allowing 3.91 YPC and 11 runs of 10-plus, with the Ravens' middle also soft at 8.54 YPA on 28 attempts versus 5.34 right.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for Ravens at Falcons, so BAL@ATL has no injury fallout to price; roles are last-three usage only, Baltimore's Henry 65 carries, Atlanta's Bijan Robinson 64, Falcons WR London 21 targets, Ravens TE Andrews 18 targets.
qb_vs_blitz: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is 0.39 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=39) and 0.33 without, and the Falcons blitz 23%, so he spends the night in the good unblitzed sample. Falcons QB Penix is the script-driver: 0.12 EPA vs blitz (n=45) and -0.41 with no blitz, against the Ravens' 31% blitz rate, so roughly seven of ten Atlanta dropbacks are the bad sample and the ball should stay on the ground.

picks.why: Falcons RB Bijan Robinson has 64 carries and 411 yards over three games (137 a game, 6.42 YPC) against a Ravens defense at 3.91 YPC with 11 runs of 10-plus. A cut to 4.8 YPC on 20 carries is still 96, over 86.5, and Penix at -0.41 EPA unblitzed plus a 31% Baltimore blitz rate keeps Atlanta run-heavy even with Brian Robinson Jr. mixing in 35 carries.

Ravens RB Derrick Henry is 230 yards on 65 carries over three games, 76.7 a game, already under 80.5 before the matchup. The Falcons have allowed 2.99 YPC and 2 runs of 10-plus in four games, so 21.7 carries at 2.99 is about 65. Baltimore's Jackson at 0.33 EPA without a blitz does not need to force Henry into that Atlanta wall, and the Falcons blitz only 23%.
